hook.text: For years, crime in New York City slowly dropped. Then in 1994 it plummeted 40 percent in two years.

buildup.text: A tipping point is the moment when small, gradual changes suddenly trigger a massive shift in the system's behavior.

discovery.text: Malcolm Gladwell popularized the concept: epidemics, fads.

twist.text: Before the tip, everything looks stable. That is the danger.

climax.text: Watch for accumulating pressure in any system.

punchline.text: Change builds slowly, then arrives all at once.

quiz.question: What makes tipping points dangerous?
options: Pressure builds invisibly and the massive shift arrives without obvious warning
